summary: R7-NEW-CRIT-001 / R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety) are CLOSED. findings.title: R7-NEW-CRIT-001 (completeness) + R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety) closure verification: `(?:\*\*)?` optional group added — CLOSED
findings.evidence: Plan-doc line 52 now reads: `TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}`. The `(?:\*\*)?` group is positioned immediately after the slug segment `[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+` and before the mandatory single space that precedes `\(`. findings.title: Regex test — all 6 worked examples with updated regex
findings.evidence: Updated regex: `TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}`. Test results via Python re.search: (1) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; operator-bumped @abc123 at 024C; track until adopter enables Renovate cohort.' — Expected PASS, actual PASS (match: 'TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate...'; `(?:\*\*)?` consumed '**' between slug and ' (open)'). (2) 'See TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-pim (pending): adopter has prior policy-check workflow; awaiting rename PR.' — Expected PASS, actual PASS (no '**' after slug; `(?:\*\*)?` matches zero occurrences). (3) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim**' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL (no status field). (4) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL (empty description — `\S.{19,}` requires ≥20 chars). (5) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):                    ' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL (`\S` anchor rejects all-whitespace start). (6) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): short' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL ('short' = 5 chars < 20 required). Score: 6/6 correct. All examples now produce the expected result.
findings.outcome: 6/6 worked examples pass/fail correctly with the updated regex — VERIFIED

findings.title: Regex test — 3 task-specified additional edge cases
findings.evidence: Updated regex tested against 3 reviewer-specified edge cases: (1) Extra `**` markers ('**TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** ** (open): This is a long enough description here yes'): FAILS. After slug 'jrnb2024-pim', `(?:\*\*)?` consumes the first '**', leaving ' ** (open)'. The pattern then requires ' \(' (space then paren) but finds ' *' (space then asterisk) — no match. A double-bold-marker line cannot bypass the regex. (2) Multiple TF references on one line ('TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim (open): Renovate disabled here and see TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-ct (closed): second conflict ref on same line'): PASSES. Python re.search finds the first valid TF ref; the greedy `.{19,}` extends to consume the rest of the line including the second TF ref, so findall returns 1 match. Behavior is correct — a line containing at least one valid TF reference passes CI, regardless of additional prose or additional TF references appended to the line. This is the intended behavior for check-invocation-log-entry.sh: grep -E returns exit code 0 if any line matches. No false-positive concern; a line that passes must contain a well-formed TF reference. (3) Offset `**` with space before it ('TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim ** (open): This is a long enough description here yes ok'): FAILS. After slug 'jrnb2024-pim', next char is ' ' (space). `(?:\*\*)?` requires '**' IMMEDIATELY after the slug (no intervening space); since next char is ' ', the optional group matches zero occurrences. The pattern then requires ' \(' but finds ' *' — no match. The offset-** variant is correctly rejected.
findings.outcome: All 3 task-specified edge cases behave correctly — VERIFIED

findings.title: Bypass surface analysis: does `(?:\*\*)?` introduce any new bypass path?
findings.evidence: The `(?:\*\*)?` optional group matches zero or one occurrence of the literal string '**' (two asterisk characters). Exhaustive bypass analysis: (a) Single asterisk 'pim* (open)': `(?:\*\*)?` requires exactly '**' (two chars); single '*' does not satisfy this, matches zero occurrences instead; then ' \(' requires space+paren but finds '* ' — FAIL. (b) Triple asterisk 'pim*** (open)': `(?:\*\*)?` greedily matches '**' (first two chars), leaving '* (open)'; then ' \(' requires space+paren but finds '* ' — FAIL. (c) Double-bold with space 'pim** ** (open)': `(?:\*\*)?` matches '**', leaving ' ** (open)'; then ' \(' requires space+paren but finds ' *' — FAIL. (d) Uppercase type 'TF-024X-Renovate-...': `(renovate|conflict)` is case-sensitive; 'Renovate' with capital R does not match — FAIL. (e) Uppercase slug 'TF-024X-renovate-JRNB2024-pim': `[a-z0-9]+` does not match uppercase chars — FAIL. (f) Underscore in slug 'jrnb2024_pim': `[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+` requires hyphens, not underscores — FAIL. (g) Non-enumerated status '(approved)': `(open|pending|in-progress|closed)` does not include 'approved' — FAIL. (h) Wrong prefix 'TF-024Y-renovate-...': literal 'TF-024X-' required — FAIL. The `(?:\*\*)?` group is purely additive: it extends the regex to match one additional valid syntax form (the STATUS.md bold-marker convention) without removing or weakening any existing rejection criterion. No new bypass path is introduced.
findings.outcome: VERIFIED — `(?:\*\*)?` introduces zero new bypass paths

findings.title: Residual: `\S.{19,}` near-stub bypass (R7-RESIDUAL-MIN-001 — carry-forward, no change)
findings.evidence: The `\S.{19,}` pattern requires: (1) first character non-whitespace (`\S` — 1 char) + (2) at least 19 more characters of any kind (`.{19,}` — including whitespace). A description of 'x' followed by 19 spaces (20 chars total, only 1 meaningful) satisfies the regex. Python re.search confirms: 'TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim (open): x                   ' (19 trailing spaces after 'x') returns a match. This is the same finding as R7-RESIDUAL-MIN-001. The plan-doc prose ('description starting with a non-whitespace character and ≥20 characters total') is technically consistent with this behavior — it only requires the FIRST character to be non-whitespace. Deferred per the R7 reviewer note: 'no fix strictly required for fixpoint given prose alignment'. A future hardening (e.g. `\S\S.{18,}`) would close this narrow edge case. Not blocking R8 fixpoint.
findings.recommendation: No action required for R8 fixpoint. Optional future hardening: change `\S.{19,}` to `\S\S.{18,}` (requires first two chars to be non-whitespace; total still ≥20). Carry forward to v1.1 if meaningful-content audit gaps emerge in practice.
findings.outcome: CARRY-FORWARD (MIN — no change from R7; deferred per R7 reviewer note)

findings.title: Residual: regex engine unspecified — U+00A0 NBSP behavior is engine-dependent (R7 edge case 1 — carry-forward, no change)
findings.evidence: The plan-doc states `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` implements the regex 'literally' but does not specify the regex engine (grep -E vs grep -P vs awk vs Python). In Python 3 re (default Unicode mode), `\S` does NOT match U+00A0 (NON-BREAKING SPACE) — Python re.search confirms `re.match(r'\s', '\u00A0')` returns a match, meaning U+00A0 IS considered whitespace by Python re, so `\S` correctly rejects it. In POSIX ERE (grep -E), U+00A0 may or may not be treated as whitespace depending on locale (LC_ALL=C causes grep -E to treat U+00A0 as non-whitespace, which means `\S` would MATCH it — a one-char NBSP description would pass). This engine-dependence was already surfaced in R7 as MIN. No change in R8. Not blocking R8 fixpoint; requires a real-world U+00A0 description to exploit, which is unlikely in normal TF-row authoring.
findings.recommendation: Optional: specify the regex engine in the check-invocation-log-entry.sh implementation contract (e.g. 'uses grep -P for PCRE semantics' or 'uses python3 re module'). Carry forward to 024B when the script is implemented — the script implementer should document which engine is used and confirm U+00A0 behavior matches the plan-doc intent.
